text:
Elena (Finance): Quick heads up — new procurement rules go live April 1. TL;DR: manager PO auto-approval threshold moves to $5k, virtual cards required for non-contract SaaS purchases under $25k, 2-vendor quotes for purchases > $20k, and the vendor onboarding form has been updated. More below. :megaphone:

Sam (Eng): Thanks! Does the $5k auto-approve apply to contractors hiring (eng services) too?

Elena (Finance): Good Q — yes, it applies to any purchase type EXCEPT capital spend and contracts that contain custom T&Cs. For vendor/contract work we still need Sourcing review for >$10k.

Jules (Ops): Where do we request a virtual card? I used the old form last month.

Elena (Finance): Use the new "Purchase & Virtual Card" flow in Procurehub: https://redwood.example.com/procurehub/cards — it asks for cost center, approver, and TTL. Virtual cards will be the default for SaaS/non-contract vendors up to $25k.

Nadia (PM): What about recurring subscriptions that auto-renew? Do those count toward the $25k limit?

Elena (Finance): Recurring subscriptions are treated the same. If the 12-month commitment exceeds $25k we need a contract and Legal review. If it's under $25k and non-contract, virtual card is fine.

Sam (Eng): Any change to the receipt/process for managers? Means we can approve $4.5k without a PO?

Elena (Finance): Managers can auto-approve up to $5k but a PO is still required for tracking. The difference is PO approval becomes automated if the cost center has manager-level approver configured. If your team doesn't have a manager approver set up, the request will queue to Finance.

procurement-bot: New vendor onboarding form published by Elena (Finance) — https://redwood.example.com/forms/vendor-onboard — please use this for any new supplier. (form v2.1)

Jules (Ops): Submitted a vendor form just now for "BrightMetrics" (analytics) — looks straightforward.

procurement-bot: Form submission received: Jules (Ops) — ID VM-2026-0042 — auto-sent to Sourcing and Legal queue.

Raj - VP Finance: High level: this reduces small PO friction and gets us more spend on virtual cards where we can get better tracking and improved reconciliation. Please surface any edge cases this week.

Sam (Eng): Re: 2-vendor quote requirement for > $20k — is that soft if it's a single-source technical fit?

Elena (Finance): It's primarily to protect budget and negotiate better terms. If there is a technical sole-source case, document the rationale in the form and flag for Sourcing review. Sourcing can approve single-source with justification.

Nadia (PM): Will there be a short guide we can share with PMs/ICs?

Elena (Finance): Yes — one-pager and an FAQ coming tomorrow morning. I'll drop them here and in #all-hands FYI. Also running a 20-minute office hours on Thursday 11am PT to walk through the flows. :calendar: 

Sam (Eng): Great, thanks. One last ask — can finance team add the mapping for expense categories in the card UI? Makes reconciliation easier.

Elena (Finance): On it — will add the dropdown for cost categories and a short mapping table in the guide.

procurement-bot: Reminder scheduled: Procurement office hours — Thu 11:00 PT. RSVP via calendar invite sent to channel.

Raj - VP Finance: Thanks everyone — this should speed up low-dollar buys while keeping guardrails. Ping Elena directly for urgent edge cases. :thumbsup:
